title: Palestinians
capsule: Following the end of the British Mandate on 14 May 1948 and Israel's declaration of independence, the Arab population of Mandatory Palestine — approximately 1.3 million people — was left without a successor state as armies from five Arab states entered the territory. The 1948 Arab–Israeli War (al-Nakba to Palestinians) displaced approximately 700,000 Palestinian Arabs who fled or were expelled to Gaza, the West Bank, and neighboring Arab states. The armistice agreements of 1949 left the Gaza Strip under Egyptian administration and the West Bank under Jordanian control, with no Palestinian Arab state established. The dataset window of 1948–1949 captures the interstitial period between Mandate dissolution and armistice consolidation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The demographic and political events of 1948–1949 are extensively documented in UN records and British Mandatory archives; as a stateless entity during this window, the extent shown reflects pre-war Arab population distribution rather than a recognized political boundary.
